one_liner: Rust (hyper + tokio) HTTP server for Python ASGI/WSGI/RSGI apps, with higher single-worker throughput than Uvicorn and Gunicorn.
what_it_does: Granian is an application server for Python web apps. You run `pip install granian`, then `granian --interface asgi main:app` (or `wsgi`, `rsgi`), and it serves an unmodified ASGI 3 or WSGI callable. It replaces Uvicorn, Hypercorn, Gunicorn with Uvicorn workers, or uWSGI on the command line, with no changes to app code. It handles HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, TLS/mTLS and WebSockets, serves static files itself, supports the ASGI pathsend extension, and defines its own faster RSGI interface. Worker management (respawn on lifetime or RSS limits, reload, Prometheus metrics) is built in, and an experimental embeddable async server exists for ASGI/RSGI.
how_it_is_fast: hyper does the HTTP parsing, connection handling, TLS and response writing in Rust on a tokio runtime (N single-threaded runtimes in `st` mode or one N-thread runtime in `mt` mode), so Python never touches sockets or protocol state. Each request goes to a dedicated interop thread through a crossbeam channel; that thread attaches to the interpreter only while it builds the scope dict and schedules the app coroutine on the asyncio loop via `call_soon_threadsafe`. ASGI `send`/`receive` return Rust-implemented awaitables (an asyncio.Future-like object, or an already-completed one when nothing needs to wait) instead of pure-Python futures. A single-message response goes to hyper as one `Full` body, and tokio streams pathsend files without calling into Python. In the benchmark both servers run on uvloop, so the gap is the server layer, not the event loop.
when_to_use: Python ASGI services where the server's HTTP layer is a large share of per-request cost, such as fast handlers returning in-memory bodies. vs.md, 10 KB GET, one worker: 125,539 RPS vs 51,051 for Uvicorn+httptools.
WSGI apps (Django, Flask) now on Gunicorn gthread/gevent or uWSGI. vs.md, 10 KB GET at c64: Granian WSGI 125,824 RPS vs 9,175-12,204 for those servers.
Serving a Python app directly over HTTP/2. vs.md: 129,750 RPS vs 7,327 for Hypercorn.
Replacing the Gunicorn + uvicorn + httptools stack with one prebuilt wheel. Wheels cover Windows, aarch64/armv7 Linux, musl, PyPy 3.11 and free-threaded CPython 3.14t/3.15t.
Serving static assets or large files next to the app without passing them through Python (static-path mounts, pathsend streaming; ~50 KB file: 48,049 vs 30,004 RPS for Uvicorn+httptools).
when_not_to_use: I/O-bound apps whose handlers spend milliseconds waiting on a database or upstream. With 10 ms waits at c512, vs.md has Granian ASGI at 45,859 RPS vs 43,903 for Uvicorn+httptools (~4%), and 100 ms waits are a tie, so the app is the bottleneck.
Apps built on trio or gevent, or apps that need ASGI extensions Granian has not implemented (README; issue #93, TLS extension #788 still open).
Teams that need a pure-Python server they can patch or step through in a debugger. The README says Granian is not the choice for advanced debugging.
Heavy WebSocket broadcast with many clients per worker. At 32 clients, vs.md has Gunicorn's ASGI worker at 378,446 msg/s vs 338,230 for Granian ASGI and 341,182 for Granian RSGI.
Free-threaded Python in production. The README calls that support experimental and 'highly discouraged in production environments'.

integration.dependencies: click at runtime. Optional extras: uvloop/rloop/winloop, watchfiles (reload), python-dotenv, setproctitle. Source builds need a Rust toolchain and maturin>=1.14 (PyO3 0.29, hyper 1.11, tokio 1.51, rustls via tls-listener).
integration.min_toolchain: Python 3.10+ (CPython 3.10-3.15, PyPy 3.11, free-threaded 3.14t/3.15t). Rust edition 2024 for source builds; minimum rustc version not documented.
integration.platforms: Prebuilt wheels for Linux x86_64/aarch64/i686/armv7 (manylinux and musllinux), macOS x86_64/aarch64 and Windows x86_64. On Linux, multiple workers with respawn need kernel >= 5.14 and net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req enabled, or queued connections can be dropped.
integration.thread_safety: Async interfaces run Python code on each worker's asyncio loop thread. WSGI runs it on a pool of up to --blocking-threads threads that contend for the GIL. Workers are separate processes, or threads on free-threaded builds, where the app object is shared. Nothing else is documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the same ASGI 3 callable runs with no code changes, but the CLI and tuning model differ (workers, runtime threads, backpressure), trio is unsupported, some ASGI extensions are missing, and forwarded headers need the granian.utils.proxies wrappers instead of a CLI option.

gotchas: Release builds set panic="abort", so any Rust panic kills the whole worker process. CVE-2026-42544 (high; a non-ASCII Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header) and CVE-2026-42545 (an invalid WSGI response header) were single-request worker crashes, fixed in 2.7.4. Stay current and consider --respawn-failed-workers (off by default).

A plain `pip install granian` runs on stdlib asyncio, because uvloop and rloop are extras. asyncio.md shows ASGI at 85,281 RPS on asyncio vs 127,962 on uvloop. Also, raising --runtime-threads did not raise ASGI throughput in concurrency.md (st 1→4 threads: 132,067→108,238 RPS); scale with --workers.

Backpressure limits accepted connections, not requests. Behind a reverse proxy that holds many keep-alive connections, a value below that count stops new connections being accepted (README warning). Also set --workers-kill-timeout, which has no default: #875 reported workers hanging forever on shutdown, and 2.8.0/2.8.2 shipped shutdown fixes.
Passing --ssl-client-verify without --ssl-ca only logs a warning and turns client-certificate verification off (issue #853, open), so a mistyped mTLS setup accepts unauthenticated clients.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Granian when the app is Python. The catalogued siblings (Ultimate Express for Node, Qbix for PHP, Drogon, Sogou Workflow and the other C++/Go/Rust servers) cannot host an ASGI/WSGI callable. Granian is built on the catalogued hyper crate, so if the service can be written in Rust, using hyper directly avoids the Python hop entirely.
verified_claims_summary: The project's own benchmarks/vs.md (run 2026-08-05; Granian 2.8.1 built with maturin --release, jemalloc and fat LTO; Python 3.13; AMD Ryzen 7 5700X, Gentoo Linux) tested an ASGI GET returning a static 10 KB body. It used oha at 128 connections for 10 s, one worker and one runtime thread, HTTP/1.1, every async server on uvloop and Uvicorn's access log off. Granian reached 125,539 RPS vs 51,051 for Uvicorn+httptools (~2.46x) and 14,501 for Uvicorn+h11 (~8.66x). Each number is a single run, and the competing servers were whatever versions were latest on that date.
status_note: Actively maintained: 2.8.3 shipped 2026-09-14, patch releases are frequent, and fixes usually land only on the latest minor. BSD-3-Clause, installed from PyPI wheels; the README lists production users including paperless-ngx, SearXNG, Weblate, Mozilla and Sentry.
